You're doing a hands-on Playwright re-verification pass against a live dev instance of the Nxeon "Nexion" v2 customer portal, running at http://127.0.0.1:3021 on this machine. This is a real Next.js app with a real backend and real Postgres DB (sandboxed provisioning/payments only), NOT a mockup — log in for real and click through for real, don't read source and guess.

Login credentials (admin account, has real seeded services): admin@nxeon.local / iCwEt7PDdo0ne3YM
Login page: http://127.0.0.1:3021/login (form fields: input[name="email"], input[name="password"]; press Enter in the password field or find the submit button — after login it redirects to /admin for this account, but the customer portal pages under /dashboard/* are still reachable directly by URL for this account).

CONTEXT: Earlier today, a systemic CSS bug was fixed: a dark-mode-scoped block (`:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`) was structurally beating a light-mode override (`html[data-theme="light"]`) on CSS specificity for shared design tokens, causing large parts of the UI to silently render dark-mode colors even when the user had light mode selected. The fix re-scoped the light override to `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, confirmed via getComputedStyle checks on a couple of pages.

Three EARLIER audit findings were suspected — but never independently confirmed — to be side effects of this exact same root cause, and are now believed fixed:
1. VPS and Game server DETAIL pages (e.g. /dashboard/servers/<id> for a VPS, and the equivalent game server detail page) reportedly "ignored light mode entirely" — rendered dark colors regardless of the light/dark toggle.
2. The chat widget (a floating support-chat bubble/panel present on portal pages) reportedly had illegible text in light mode.
3. The cookie-consent banner reportedly had broken/illegible styling in light mode.

YOUR JOB: For each of these three, actually toggle the site to light mode (there's a moon/sun icon toggle in the top header — click it to switch themes; this sets `data-theme` on <html>), navigate to the relevant page/component, and take a screenshot. Then separately verify via `page.evaluate(() => getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--color-bg'))` (or inspect an actual rendered element's background/text color, e.g. `getComputedStyle(el).color` and `.backgroundColor`) that the colors are genuinely light-mode-appropriate (light background, dark-enough text for contrast) rather than dark-mode leaking through.

For #1 (server detail pages): find a real VPS server and a real game server owned by this admin account (check /dashboard/services or /dashboard/servers for a list) and open each one's detail page in light mode.
For #2 (chat widget): find and open the chat widget on any portal page in light mode.
For #3 (cookie-consent banner): this may only appear on first visit / if no consent cookie is set yet — you may need to clear cookies/use a fresh browser context to make it appear, then switch to light mode (or set the theme before it appears) and check it.

For each of the three, report: STILL BROKEN (with the specific colors/contrast problem you observed and a screenshot path) or CONFIRMED FIXED (with the computed color values proving it). Do not fix anything yourself — this is a verification-only pass. Do not fabricate results — if you can't get a page/component to appear or can't log in, say so plainly rather than guessing. Save any screenshots to /tmp/claude-0/-/a847f019-50a6-4b60-bcba-1133f2a3ca8a/scratchpad/ (create it if needed, or use /tmp if that's unavailable to you). Playwright test scripts you write must live inside /opt/nxeon-v2 for module resolution to work (any subdirectory is fine) — delete them when you're done. Keep your final report under 400 words, structured as three clear verdicts.
